stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Proper means universally closed, separated, and of finite type, jointly.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is proper,
\item for every scheme $Z$ and every morphism $Z \to Y$
the projection $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is proper,
\item for every affine scheme $Z$ and every morphism $Z \to Y$
the projection $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is proper,
\item there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is proper, and
\item there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is proper.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$.
conclusions:
for every scheme $Z$ and every morphism $Z \to Y$
the projection $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is proper,

for every affine scheme $Z$ and every morphism $Z \to Y$
the projection $Z \times_Y X \to Z$ is proper,

there exists a scheme $V$ and a surjective \'etale morphism
$V \to Y$ such that $V \times_Y X \to V$ is proper, and

there exists a Zariski covering $Y = \bigcup Y_i$ such that
each of the morphisms $f^{-1}(Y_i) \to Y_i$ is proper.

reason: Properness is by definition separated, finite type, and universally closed; each property has the same étale-local scheme-test equivalences proved earlier, so their conjunction gives the five properness tests.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $B$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $B$.
If $X$ is universally closed over $B$ and $f$ is surjective then
$Y$ is universally closed over $B$. In particular, if also $Y$ is
separated and of finite type over $B$, then $Y$ is proper over $B$.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Proper means universally closed, separated, and of finite type, jointly.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let
$$
\xymatrix{
X \ar[rr]_h \ar[rd]_f & & Y \ar[ld]^g \\
& B
}
$$
be a commutative diagram of morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X \to B$ is a proper morphism,
\item $Y \to B$ is separated and locally of finite type,
\end{enumerate}
Then the scheme theoretic image $Z \subset Y$ of $h$
is proper over $B$ and $X \to Z$ is surjective.
conclusions:
the scheme theoretic image $Z \subset Y$ of $h$
is proper over $B$ and $X \to Z$ is surjective.

reason: Proper X→B and separated locally finite-type Y→B make h:X→Y quasi-compact. Its scheme-theoretic image Z receives a dense image of X, which is also closed by universal closedness of h, hence X→Z is surjective. The preceding proper-image lemma yields Z proper over B.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is separated,
\item $\Delta_{X/Y} : X \to X \times_Y X$ is universally closed, and
\item $\Delta_{X/Y} : X \to X \times_Y X$ is proper.
\end{enumerate}
